questions.question_text: The energy required to remove an electron from the highest occupied atomic orbital is known as
questions.answer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove the most loosely held electron from the outermost shell of an atom.

questions.question_text: The most electronegative element possess which of the following the electronic configuration?
questions.answer: Elements with ns2 np5 configuration include fluorine, the most electronegative element.

questions.question_text: Identify the least stable ion amongst the following:
questions.answer: Be- is highly unstable due to the unfavorable addition of an electron to an already filled 2s orbital.

questions.question_text: The property Atomic size in the periodic table _______ on moving down a group
questions.answer: Atomic size increases down a group due to addition of new shells.

questions.question_text: Loss of small molecule from original organic molecule is
questions.answer: Elimination reactions involve removal of a small molecule (like H2O, HX) from the reactant.

questions.question_text: Drugs that are used to diagnose, cure and prevent disease are called
questions.answer: Pharmaceutical drugs are medicines used for treatment, diagnosis, or prevention of diseases.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Synthesis of a commonly used drug molecule

questions.question_text:
The most suitable reagent for the following transformation is
[Image: Cyclohexene -> Adipic acid (HOOC-(CH2)4-COOH)]
questions.answer: Hot acidic KMnO4 causes oxidative cleavage of double bonds, converting cyclohexene to adipic acid.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Introduction to reactions involving oxidation/ring openings

questions.question_text: Identify the reducing agent from the following
questions.answer: LiAlH4 is a strong reducing agent commonly used in organic chemistry for reduction reactions.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Introduction to reactions involving reduction

questions.question_text: Which of the following method is used to remove hardness from water sample.
questions.answer: Demineralization (or ion exchange) removes all dissolved minerals, including ions causing hardness.

questions.question_text: The exhausted cationic resins are regenerated by
questions.answer: Cation exchange resins are regenerated by washing with acid, which restores the H+ sites.

questions.question_text: Permanent hardness of water is due to calcium
questions.answer: Permanent hardness is caused by chlorides and sulphates of calcium/magnesium, which do not decompose on boiling.

questions.question_text: Water can be sterilized by
questions.answer: Chlorine is commonly used as a disinfectant in water treatment to kill bacteria and pathogens.

questions.question_text: Hypophosphite is used as a reducing agent in
questions.answer: Hypophosphite acts as the reducing agent in electroless plating, facilitating metal deposition without electricity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following metal will form non-porous oxide layer?
questions.answer: Aluminium forms a non-porous, protective oxide layer that prevents further corrosion.

questions.question_text: Anhydrous inorganic metal surface in the absence of moisture exhibits
questions.answer: Dry corrosion occurs in absence of moisture, typically due to direct reaction with atmospheric gases.

questions.question_text: When the hydrogen over voltage is low, the corrosion rate will be
questions.answer: A low hydrogen overvoltage facilitates hydrogen evolution and thus increases corrosion rate.

questions.question_text: Nernst glower is the source of
questions.answer: Nernst glower is a source used for producing infrared radiation in spectroscopy instruments.

questions.question_text: Reference electrode used in potentiometric titration is
questions.answer: Calomel electrode is a very common reference electrode due to its stable and reproducible potential.

questions.question_text: Finger print region in IR spectroscopy is ____
questions.answer: The fingerprint region of IR spectra is from 1400 to 900 cm-1, unique for each molecule.

questions.question_text: Hydrogen bonding in a molecule can be detected easily using.
questions.answer: IR spectroscopy is very sensitive to vibrations affected by hydrogen bonding in molecules.
